question:
The area of rectangle \(ABCD\) is \(72\) square units. If point \(A\) and the midpoints of \(\overline{BC}\) and \(\overline{CD}\) are joined to form a triangle, the area of that triangle is

[Figure 1](figures/2000_AMC_8_Q25_question_fig1.svg)
solution:
Let \(M\) be the midpoint of \(BC\), and let \(N\) be the midpoint of \(CD\). The desired triangle \(AMN\) leaves three right triangles at the corners of the rectangle. Their bases and heights lie along the rectangle's sides, so their areas are easier to calculate.

Triangle \(ABM\) has base \(AB\) and height \(BC/2\). Since \(AB\cdot BC=72\), its area is
\[
\frac12\cdot AB\cdot\frac{BC}{2}=\frac{72}{4}=18.
\]
Similarly, triangle \(ADN\) has base \(DN=CD/2\) and height \(AD\), so its area is also \(72/4=18\).

Triangle \(CMN\) has perpendicular legs \(CM=BC/2\) and \(CN=CD/2\). Its area is
\[
\frac12\cdot\frac{BC}{2}\cdot\frac{CD}{2}=\frac{72}{8}=9.
\]
These three corner triangles and triangle \(AMN\) fill the rectangle without overlapping interiors. Therefore the desired area is
\[
72-18-18-9=\boxed{27}
\]
square units, choice \(\mathrm{B}\).
